exact_evidence.finding: The Hebrew opening וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם frames a reparation-offering manual covering slaughter, blood, fat, altar disposition, priestly consumption, place, and most-holy status.
כַּחַטָּאת כָּאָשָׁם תּוֹרָה אַחַת לָהֶם explicitly coordinates purification and reparation offerings, while its priestly-share clause continues the disposition concern of Lev.7.6.
The text broadens to priestly allocations from burnt and grain offerings: hide in 7.8, prepared grain portions in 7.9, and shared grain portions in 7.10.
No Masoretic open-section marker occurs after Lev.7.6; an open-section marker occurs after Lev.7.10. This supports 7.1-10 as one witnessed section with a genuine subordinate seam at 7.7.
WEB inserts a paragraph before 7.7, exposing the functional shift, but project strategy treats paragraphing as evidence rather than boundary authority.

strongest_counterevidence: Lev.7.7-10 forms a coherent cross-offering allocation sequence distinct from the reparation-specific procedure in 7.1-6. A physical split would yield two usable children, and the WEB paragraph at 7.7 supports that reading.
translation_hebrew_caveats: אָשָׁם may be rendered guilt, trespass, or reparation offering; חַטָּאת may be rendered sin or purification offering. English labels must not determine the boundary.
תּוֹרָה אַחַת לָהֶם means one governing instruction/law for the paired offerings and makes 7.7 both retrospective and coordinative.
The conjunction-led sequence in 7.8-10 supports an allocation list, but it does not supply a new speech frame or Masoretic section opening.
WEB and MT/OSHB versification resynchronize at Lev.7.1.

residual_dissent.position: Physically split at Lev.7.7 because actor/function broadens from one offering procedure to a cross-offering allocation digest.
residual_dissent.why_not_adopted: The reparation-share clause in 7.7 continues 7.6, OSHB supplies no section break after 7.6, and explicit subordinate mapping prevents the broader allocation sequence from being buried.

human_external_ai_hold.reason: The internal map and typed relations preserve both readings without coverage loss or a top-level rewrite.
